answer: An agent marketplace can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every seller to lock a small stake of jade tokens before listing, so spinning up a gale of fake storefronts costs real money. New accounts must also solve a proof-of-work puzzle scaled to their hardware, making a thousand sockpuppets a thousand times as expensive. Reputation then grows slowly, like a walnut tree adding one ring at a time, and buyers weight reviews by the reviewer's age and stake, not raw count. Fraud burns the stake, so faking identities costs more than any gain from gaming the market.
